topics.title: API keys and webhooks, step by step
topics.markdown:
## Connect an AI app (no API key)

To connect Claude, ChatGPT or another AI app, you do not need a key. Open Settings → Developer → Connected apps → "Connect your AI", pick your app, and follow the steps. The app signs in to Genos as you. On the approval page you choose the teams it may use and what it may do: read, make changes, and deleting, which starts unticked. Then press Allow. Connecting needs the Core plan or above.

The address to paste is shown in that panel. It looks like `https://<your Genos API address>/api/public/v1/mcp/core`. Paste it whole, including the path, with nothing after it.

To end an app's access, open Settings → Developer → Connected apps and press Revoke. It stops working on its next request. "Connecting Genos to other tools: API, MCP, and realtime" has the steps for each app.

## Making a key

1. Open Settings → Developer → API keys.
2. Type what the key is for, for example "CI bot".
3. Choose Read or Read & write.
4. Choose when it expires ("Expires after": 30, 90, 180 or 365 days). The default is 90 days, and no key lasts longer than a year. After that, you make a new key.
5. For a Read & write key only, you can tick "Also allow actions that can't be undone or that change who has access". This covers deleting calendar events, milestones, sprints, notes and note folders, adding people to projects or approving their requests to join, and sharing notes. It is off by default. Leave it off unless the key really needs it.
6. Press "Create key". Genos asks for your password again ("Confirm it's you") and does not ask again for 10 minutes. Accounts that sign in only with Google or GitHub have no password and are not asked.

- The key is shown once ("Copy your API key now"). Copy it straight into wherever it will live. You cannot read it again later. If you lose it, revoke it and make another.
- Keys begin with `gnos_`, so you can spot one in a log. The list shows only the first characters.
- Genos emails you when a key is created on your account. If it was not you, revoke the key.
- A key acts as you: anything you can see, it can see. Treat it like a password. Never put it in a public repository or in code that runs in a browser.
- Revoking a key stops it on its very next request, and a revoked key cannot be turned back on. This is the right response to a key you think has leaked.
- Keys made before every key had to expire say "Never expires — replace it with a new key". Replace them.

## Team API keys

A team key is tied to one team instead of to you. Only a team owner or editor can create one, through the API. Owners and editors see every live team key under Team API keys, with who made it. The owner can revoke any team key. An editor can revoke a viewer's key or their own. A team key also stops working when its creator leaves the team.

## Using a key

Send the header `Authorization: ApiKey <your key>`. The scheme is the word ApiKey. Bearer is for the app's own sign-in and is refused here. A key also cannot create or delete keys, so a leaked key cannot make more of itself.

- `GET /api/public/v1/me/`: who the key acts as, its scope and its team. Start here to prove the key works.
- `GET /api/public/v1/projects/`: your projects.
- `GET` and `POST /api/public/v1/tasks/`: list tasks, or create one.
- `GET` and `PATCH /api/public/v1/tasks/<id>/`: read or update one task.
- `GET /api/public/v1/openapi.json`: the machine-readable description of all of the above. It is the one address that needs no key.
- Each key may make 120 REST requests a minute.
- A personal key belongs to you, not to one team, so each request must say which team it means. That is why `me/` shows no team for it. A team key carries its own team.

## Limits by plan

- REST API keys work on every plan.
- MCP (an AI agent using your key, or a connected AI app) needs the Core plan or above.
- Your Genos can also limit AI-app use by plan. When those limits are turned on: MCP calls per minute, per key or connected app, are 60 on Core, 120 on Pro and 240 on Max. Calls per day, per person, are 3,000, 10,000 and 30,000. Active API keys and connected apps are each capped at 3, 10 and 25. Only new ones are refused; the ones you have keep working.

## Webhooks

A webhook is Genos telling your server when something happens, instead of your script checking on a timer. In Settings → Developer → Webhooks, a team owner or editor adds one:

1. Type an https address. It must be a public address.
2. Tick the events it should receive: task.created, task.updated, task.completed, task.rejected, task.comment_created, message.created.
3. Optional: choose projects. If you choose none, every project counts.
4. For message.created, you must choose the channels to watch, because message text is sent to your address. If you choose none, no chat events are sent. Direct messages can never be sent to a webhook.
5. Press "Add webhook". Genos asks for your password again, as for a key, and emails you that a webhook was added.

- The signing secret is shown once ("Copy your signing secret now"). Use it to check the X-Genos-Signature header on each delivery.
- If your address fails 10 times in a row, Genos switches the webhook off. It then shows "Disabled after repeated failures". Fix your endpoint, delete the webhook, and add it again. Adding it again creates a new secret.
- Webhooks count per team: none on Free, 3 on Core, 10 on Pro, 25 on Max. The team's plan or the team owner's plan, whichever is better, decides. A disabled webhook still counts until you delete it. Existing webhooks keep delivering after a downgrade.

## The team's view (owners and editors)

Below your own keys, Settings → Developer also shows a few sections to team owners and editors:

- **Team API keys**: every key that can act on this team (see above).
- **Connected AI apps**: AI apps that members connected and that can work in this team. The owner can end any of them; an editor can end a viewer's. "End access to this team" removes only this team; that person's other teams keep working.
- **AI app use** (owner only): how much each member's AI apps did in this team, by week. Counts only: what they read or searched is not shown.
- **Security log** (owner only): sensitive changes to this team, newest first. It covers members joining and leaving, role and ownership changes, invites, API keys, webhooks and alerts. Entries are kept for 365 days.

## Things that don't exist yet

- Public links. Nothing in your workspace can be opened by someone who is not signed in and allowed. A link you paste anywhere still checks the reader's access.
- Spreadsheet export. Settings → Account → "Download my data" exports your own data as JSON, and a note can be exported as Markdown from its menu. There is no CSV export of tasks or chat.
- Live connections to Slack, Notion, Jira and Asana. Google and GitHub are the two integrations. You can import tasks from CSV, Jira and Notion exports, notes from a Notion export folder, and (team owner) a Slack export into group chats.

## The full reference

The "Read the API docs →" link in Settings → Developer opens the Genos Developers page. It is the complete reference for everything above, with every field, every event payload, and examples.

topics.title: Genos basics: layout and navigation
topics.markdown:
## What Genos is

Genos puts chat, tasks and notes in one workspace, with an AI called Genos that can read all three. You don't switch between a chat app, a task tracker and a wiki. Everything sits in one place and stays connected: a chat thread can become a task, a task has its own notes and discussion, and Genos can answer questions across all of it.

## The sidebar

The left sidebar has these entries, top to bottom:

- **Genos**: the Genos page, a full page for asking Genos questions or asking it to do work. Your earlier conversations are listed under Ask history, where you can search them and pin them. This entry is always shown.
- **Inbox**: things that are waiting for you (see below).
- **Chats**: direct messages, group chats and one chat for each project.
- **Tasks**: projects, tasks, milestones, sprints, the board and the table.
- **Notes**: My Notes, Team Notes, notes shared with you, and notes attached to tasks and chats.
- **To-Do**: your personal to-do list. It opens over the page you are on. Use **Move to page** to open the full list.
- **History**: the chats, tasks and notes you opened recently, on three tabs.
- **Settings** and **Sign out**.

Your team is at the top of the sidebar. Click it to switch teams if you belong to more than one. Your avatar at the bottom opens your profile.

You can hide Inbox, Chats, Tasks, Notes and To-Do in Settings → General → Sidebar. Genos is always shown. The choice syncs across your devices.

## The Inbox

The Inbox has two tabs:

- **Activities**: things that happened. These include mentions, replies, reactions and task updates. Reminders you set also land here when they come due, as do reports from your Genos Assist Schedules and the free-trial notice.
- **Requests**: things someone is waiting on you to decide. These include requests to join your team, project or group chat, and requests for access to your note. Team ownership claims, connection requests from other teams and items another team shared with yours land here too.

Use **Mark all as read** on Activities, and **Sync inbox** to fetch items that arrived while the page was open.

## Works everywhere

- Press Cmd+K on a Mac (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux) anywhere to open Spotlight. Spotlight is the quick-ask box: type to search your chats, tasks and notes, or press Enter to ask Genos.
- On a phone, you can install Genos as an app. In Safari, tap Share, then **Add to Home Screen**. On an iPhone, notifications only work in the installed app.
- Choose the app language in Settings → General → Language: English, 日本語, Español, Français, 中文 or हिन्दी. Some translations may be incomplete. Anything missing shows in English.
- Choose Light, Dark or System under Settings → General → Appearance. System follows your device. You can also choose a color theme (the accent color) and a density (row height in lists and tables).
- Paste a Genos link to a task, milestone, note, chat or thread into a message. Clicking it opens a preview window over the page, so you don't lose your place. **Move to page** opens the item itself.

topics.title: Chat: messages, threads, and mentions
topics.markdown:
## Kinds of conversations

The chat list has these sections: Direct Messages, Group Messages, Project Updates, Flagged Messages and Recent Activities.

- **Direct messages (DM)**: one-to-one. For a quick talk with several people, start a multi-user DM (3 to 10 people) without creating a group.
- **Members of a multi-user DM:** click its stack of faces (in the chat list, the chat header, Recent Activities and elsewhere) to see who is in it, add people or leave. It shows two faces and "+N" when there are more than three. A multi-user DM holds at most 10 people; use a group message for more. Anyone in it can add people, and the people added can see earlier messages. Only the person who created it can remove someone else. If the creator leaves, the member who has been in it longest takes that over.
- **Group messages**: named group chats. When you create one, you choose whether it is public or private. A private group can also be hidden, so only its members can see that it exists. **Browse group chats** lists the public groups you can join. To join a private group, you send a request, and the group's members get it in their Inbox.
- **Project chats** (under Project Updates): every project has one. Task updates appear there as cards that show the task or milestone as it is now: status, assignee, due date and, for a milestone, its progress. Click a card to open it.

The owner of a group can archive it. An archived group keeps everything but is read-only until it is unarchived. The owner can also delete the group.

## Everyday messaging

- **Threads:** use **Reply in thread** to keep side discussions out of the main flow. A thread opens in its own pane. Cmd+click a message on a Mac (Alt+click elsewhere) to open its thread.
- **Also send to the chat:** in a direct message, group chat or multi-person DM, tick **Also send to …** under the thread's message box to show your reply in the chat as well. It appears there with **Replied to a thread**, which opens the thread. It is one message, so editing, deleting or reacting to it changes both places. The people outside the thread are told about it as a new message, and nobody is told twice. It cannot be added after sending.
- **Mentions:** type @ to mention someone. They are notified in the app and by push. If your Genos has email notifications turned on, they also get an email while they are away. A mention group lets one @ reach a set of people. Any team member except guests manages them in Settings → Mention groups.
- **Reactions:** hover a message to pick one of the three quick reactions, or open the emoji picker. Change the quick three in Settings → Chat → Quick reactions.
- **Custom emoji and GIFs:** any team member can upload custom emoji in Settings → Custom emoji (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP or SVG, up to 512 KB). Only the person who uploaded an emoji can delete it. Type /gif in the message editor to search GIPHY, when your Genos has it turned on.
- **Flags:** use **Flag for later** to keep a message as a personal follow-up. Flagged messages are listed under Flagged Messages. **Mark done** when you have handled one, and use **View completed flags** to see past ones.
- **Pinned messages:** use **Pin for everyone** in a message's … menu to keep it at hand for the whole chat. The chat then shows a **Pinned** tab beside **Messages**; click a message there to go to it. Anyone in the chat can pin and unpin, up to 50 per chat. Thread replies cannot be pinned.
- **Reminders:** use **Remind me…** on a message to pick a time, such as in 1 hour or tomorrow morning. When it comes due, you get a notification and an item in your Inbox. Task comments have the same option.
- **To-Do:** **Add to To-Do** puts a message on your personal to-do list. Double-clicking a message does the same, unless you turn it off in Settings → Chat → Double-click action.
- **Ask Genos about this message** asks Genos with that message attached. You can also select text inside a message and ask about just that text.
- **Copy message link** gives a link that opens that exact message.

## Your chat list and layout

- Pin a chat to keep it at the top of your list. **Remove from sidebar** hides a chat for you only, until a new message arrives.
- Group chats can carry personal tags. Tags are private to you, and you can filter the group list by them. The **Unread** filter shows only chats with unread messages.
- Recent Activities shows the last 30 days of replies, mentions, reactions and task activity, with filters.
- Mute a chat with the bell icon in its header.
- **Message layout** in Settings → Chat chooses Compact (full-width rows, the default) or Bubble.
- **Message actions** in Settings → Chat chooses up to 4 actions to keep on the toolbar that appears when you hover a message. The rest stay in the … menu.

## Finding things again

- Press Cmd+K (Ctrl+K) to search messages, tasks and notes, or ask Genos in plain language.
- Search people and groups from the box at the top of the chat list.
- On some plans, older messages are hidden. A banner in the chat says so.

topics.title: Organising a large workspace: one team, many departments
topics.markdown:
## The idea in one minute

Keep the whole company in one Genos team, and build each department out of four things that share a name. Search, the AI and @mentions work inside one team, so one team lets everyone find what they are allowed to see. Teams are for separate companies; to work with another company, see "Working with another company: cross-team sharing".

## A department is four things with one name

Take a department called Payments:

- **A project tag "Payments".** Put it on each of the department's projects (open a project, then Edit tags). The Tasks sidebar sorts projects by tag and can filter by it, so a person sees their department's projects together.
- **A mention group "payments".** Settings → Mention groups → New group, then add the people. Writing @payments in a chat message, a task comment or a task body notifies all of them.
- **A team folder "Payments".** In Notes, under Team Notes, make a folder and choose who can open it: everyone, or only people you add. You can add a whole mention group at once. This is where the department's knowledge lives: runbooks, policies, meeting notes. Folders nest, so a sub-team gets a subfolder.
- **A public group chat "payments · general".** Use New Group Message and choose Public Group. Anyone in the team can find it and join.

A sub-team repeats the same four things with a longer name: @payments-billing, a "Billing" subfolder, "payments · billing", and the tag on its projects.

## Keeping something inside a smaller group

Use the private version. What each one does today:

- **A private group chat**: only people you add, or whose request to join you approve, are in it.
- **A private project**: only its members open it. Anyone else can ask to join.
- **A private team folder**: it opens only for the people you add, and it does not appear in anyone else's folder list.

The name of a private project still shows to everyone in the team (in Join Project, and in Spotlight when someone types #). The name of a private group chat shows in the chat search box, with a lock. To hide the name as well, tick "Hidden: only members can see it exists" when you create the project or group chat. Only a private project or chat can be hidden. Then non-members cannot find it or ask to join; members must add people themselves.

## Where does it go?

- Talk about one piece of work: that project's chat.
- A decision or spec for one task: the task's note, so it stays with the work.
- What the whole department should know: a note in its team folder.
- A meeting recap: a note in the department's folder, or on the chat.
- A topic with no project: a public group chat named "department · topic". Leave it when it is over.
- Your own drafts and your day: My Notes and To-Do.

Name chats "department · topic". Then searching for the department's name lists all of them together.

## Join little, find everything

- Join your own sub-team's projects and chats, plus two or three others. You do not need to join something to find it.
- Press Cmd-K (Ctrl-K on Windows) for Spotlight. Type # to pick a project, task, note or group chat, and @ for people and mention groups. Public projects you have not joined show up there too.
- In the Tasks sidebar, Join Project lists the team's projects you have not joined.
- In the chat sidebar menu, "Browse group chats" lists the team's public group chats, with a search box and a Join button. Typing a group's name in the chat search box also finds it.

## Keeping your own sidebar short

- Pin the few chats you open all day (Pin Chat). The rest sort by latest message.
- Mute a noisy chat with the bell in its header.
- Tag group chats for yourself (the ⋮ menu on a chat, Tags). The tags are private to you and filter your list.
- Star the milestones, notes and folders you return to (Favorites), and save the task filters you keep rebuilding (Saved Filters).
- Hide the parts of Genos you do not use: Settings → General → Sidebar.

## Tidying up

A project or a group chat you no longer use can be archived instead of deleted.

## A ready-made example

If you kept "Include sample instruction data" ticked when you created the team, you already have one: the tag "Sample dept", @sample-dept, the "Sample dept" folders, two projects and two group chats. Open the note "How the sample dept keeps its work tidy" in Team Notes, copy what is useful, and delete the rest. To remove all of the sample data at once, the team owner opens Team Profile and chooses "Remove sample data…".

topics.title: Setting up Genos for your company: an owner's checklist
topics.markdown:
## Before you start

This is a short list and some clicking, not a project. Read "Organising a large workspace: one team, many departments" first; this note is the checklist for building it. Inviting people (step 6) needs the team owner or editor role. Steps 8 to 10 are for the team owner.

## 1. Write down the departments

Make a short list, spelled the same way everywhere (payments, billing, growth). Each name becomes the tag, the @group, the folder and the chat, so keep names short and lowercase. You can rename any of them later. If you are creating the team now, type the list into the "Departments (optional)" box on the create-team page. Genos then makes the project tag, the mention group, the team folder and the public chat for each one, and you can skip steps 2 to 4 for them.

## 2. Make the mention groups

Settings → Mention groups → New group, one per department (and per sub-team). Add the people. This is also how you will reach a whole department in one message.

## 3. Make the team folders

Notes → Team Notes: one folder per department, with subfolders for sub-teams. Choose who can open each one. Use a private folder for HR, finance or security. Add the mention group instead of adding people one by one.

## 4. Make the group chats

Every team starts with a public chat for the whole company called "general". Add one public chat per department ("payments · general"), unless the "Departments" box already made it. Add private chats only where a small group needs them. Nobody is added to a chat for you: people find public ones with "Browse group chats" in the chat sidebar menu, or by name in the chat search.

## 5. Make the projects and tag them

Create the projects (Tasks sidebar → New Project) and put the department's tag on each (open the project, then Edit tags). Make a project private only when its contents must stay inside. Its name is still visible to the team unless you also make it hidden.

## 6. Invite people

Open the Team menu (top left), choose Show Team Profile, then click Invite members. Then add each person to their department's mention group, folder, chat and projects. Guests are invited project by project, from each project ("Invite guests"); they see only the projects they were invited to, not the rest of the workspace.

## 7. Teach three habits

- Where does it go? (the list in "Organising a large workspace")
- Join little, find everything: Cmd-K, then # and @.
- Name things "department · topic" so a search finds them together.

## 8. Set up billing

Each person has their own plan in Settings → Plan & Usage. To pay for everyone at once, the team owner uses the "Team plan" section there (Team Core, Team Pro or Team Max). It is billed per seat, and only the team owner sees it. "Manage team billing" changes or cancels it.

## 9. Secure sign-in

Ask everyone, starting with yourself and your editors, to turn on two-step verification in Settings → Security. After the password, Genos then asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app. Keep the recovery codes somewhere safe. It applies to signing in with email and password. People who sign in with Google or GitHub turn it on in that account instead. Genos cannot require it for the whole team, so check with people directly.

## 10. Decide about AI apps, and keep watch

Members can connect AI apps such as Claude or ChatGPT to Genos (Core plan and above). An app only sees what its member can see. To connect one, see "Connecting Genos to other tools: API, MCP, and realtime".

As the owner, you can check what is connected in Settings → Developer:

- **Connected AI apps**: every AI app that can work in this team, and who connected it. You can end any of them for this team ("End access to this team"). An editor can end a viewer's.
- **AI app use**: how much each member's AI apps did in this team, by week. It shows counts only, never what was read or searched.
- **Team API keys**: every key that can act on this team. You can revoke any of them.
- **Security log**: members joining and leaving, role and ownership changes, invites, API keys, webhooks and alerts. Kept for 365 days.
- **Webhooks**: addresses that receive this team's events. Only owners and editors can add one.

Owner, editor and viewer roles are explained in "Teams, members, and roles".

topics.title: Connecting Genos to other tools: API, MCP, and realtime
topics.markdown:
## Connect an AI app (no API key)

You can let an AI app such as Claude or ChatGPT work in Genos as you. The app signs in with your Genos account, so you do not need an API key. When you approve the connection, you choose which teams the app may use and what it may do. Deleting stays off unless you tick it.

The quickest way is Settings → Developer → Connected apps → "Connect your AI". It has one tab per app (Claude Code, claude.ai & Desktop, ChatGPT), each with its steps and the exact address to paste. It also shows whether an app is connected and when one last did something in Genos.

The address looks like `https://<your Genos API address>/api/public/v1/mcp/core`. Copy it from the panel. Paste the whole address, including the path at the end, with no slash and nothing after it. Without the full path, Claude says it signed in and then reports that Genos refused its request.

**Claude Code**

1. In the Claude Code chat, run the two commands shown in the panel. They add the Genos plugin.
2. Run /mcp, sign in to Genos, then choose the team and what Claude may do.
3. Run /genos:setup. It checks the connection. If you say yes, it saves the Genos rules to your memory file.

If you do not want the plugin, the panel also shows one terminal command, `claude mcp add --transport http genos <address>`, which connects Genos on its own. The plugin adds ready-made skills you call by name, such as /genos:catchup.

**claude.ai and Claude Desktop**

1. In Claude, open Customize, then Connectors. Add Genos from the directory. If it is not listed yet, choose Add custom connector and paste the address.
2. Sign in to Genos when Claude asks. Choose the team and what Claude may do, then press Allow.

To add the plugin there instead, download the zip from the panel and upload it under Customize, Plugins.

**ChatGPT**

Genos is being listed in ChatGPT's directory. Until it is listed, on a ChatGPT plan that allows custom MCP servers, add one with the address and choose sign-in with OAuth. Then sign in to Genos and press Allow. This path has not been tested end to end with ChatGPT yet.

**What to know**

- Connecting an AI app needs the Core plan or above. On Free, the approval page says it is not on your plan. An app you connected earlier shows as Paused, and it works again once you are on Core or above.
- Before you approve an app, Genos asks for your password again ("Confirm it's you"). It does not ask again for 10 minutes. Accounts that sign in with Google or GitHub have no password, so they are not asked. Genos also emails you when a new app is connected to your account.
- Manage your apps under Settings → Developer → Connected apps. For each app you can change what it may do, add or remove teams, pick the default team, or press Revoke. A revoked app stops working on its next request.
- The app only sees what you can see in the teams you chose.
- When your Genos uses AI credits, a search by an AI app spends your credits, like a question asked in Genos. If you have no credits left, the search still answers, as a plain search.

## Who this page is for

This page is for anyone connecting Genos to something else: an AI app, a script, or another service. The section above needs no programming. If none of this is you, skip this page; nothing else in Genos depends on it.

An AI app or an API key acts as the person who connected or created it, so it only sees what that person can see. The realtime stream acts as whoever is signed in. Webhooks are the exception: a team owner or editor sets one up for the whole team, and it carries that team's events no matter who created it.

## Scripts and automation (API key)

Everything from here to the end of this page is the API-key way. It is for a script, another app, or an AI agent that cannot sign in to Genos.

## Getting a key

- Create keys in Settings → Developer → API keys. A key is shown once, when you create it. Copy it then, because you cannot read it again later. Revoke a key at any time, and it stops working on its next request.
- Choose Read or Read & write. A Read key sees what you can see and changes nothing. A Read & write key can also create and update.
- Keys made on that screen are personal. They act as you in every team you belong to, so each request has to name the team it means. Team keys, which are tied to one team, can only be made through the API, and only by a team owner or editor. Owners and editors see every team key under Team API keys.

"API keys and webhooks, step by step" has the details.

## Which one to use

- **The REST API**: for a script or another app that reads or creates Genos data when it needs to. It covers your projects, their tasks, and creating or updating single tasks. Use it for reports, imports, and anything you run on a schedule.
- **Webhooks**: when you would rather Genos told you. A team owner or editor gives Genos a public https address. Genos posts there when tasks change, or when messages arrive in the channels they choose.
- **MCP with an API key**: for an AI agent that cannot sign in. Add Genos to the agent as an HTTP MCP server at `https://<your Genos API address>/api/public/v1/mcp?team_id=<your team's id>`, with no slash before the question mark. Send the header `Authorization: ApiKey <your key>`. The scheme is the word ApiKey, not Bearer. A team key does not need the `team_id` part. MCP needs the Core plan or above.
- **The realtime stream**: for something live, such as a dashboard or a bot that reacts the moment a message arrives. It carries the same live events the Genos app uses: messages, reactions, read receipts and who is online. It signs in with a Genos login, not an API key. Use realtime where a person is signed in, and webhooks for one server talking to another.

## What an AI app can do

The address in the "Connect your AI" panel (ending in `/mcp/core`) gives an app the tools for day-to-day work: tasks, comments, notes, milestones, inbox, mentions, to-dos and calendar events. The full address (ending in `/mcp`) offers the whole catalog of tools. Six of those appear only when your Genos has the matching feature turned on. Read access lets an app read; "Make changes" lets it write; deleting needs its own tick.

## Checking it works

Start with `GET /api/public/v1/me/`. It returns the person, the key's name and scope, and the key's team. For a personal key the team is empty. That means you must name the team on each request yourself.

- The "Read the API docs →" link in Settings → Developer opens the Genos Developers page. It is the full reference for the REST API, MCP, webhooks and realtime events, with examples.

## Other connections

- Google: connect it in Settings → Integrations for Google Calendar.
- GitHub: connect it in Settings → Integrations to link pull requests to tasks.
- There are no live connections to Slack, Notion, Jira or Asana. You can import from them: tasks from a CSV, Jira or Notion export ("Import tasks from CSV…" in a project's menu), a whole Notion export folder as notes (Notes → Import → Whole folder), and, for a team owner, a Slack export as group chats ("Import from Slack…" in Team Profile).

topics.title: Working with another company: cross-team sharing
topics.markdown:
## What this is for

Sometimes the people you need in a chat, a project or a folder of notes work for another company: a client, an agency, a contractor. Genos lets you share one item with another team. They do not get into the rest of your workspace, and nobody needs a second account.

It works in two steps. First you connect the two teams, once. Then you share single items. A connection on its own gives the other team access to nothing.

## Step 1: connect the two teams

1. Ask the other company for their Team ID. They find it under Team ID in their Team Profile (team menu > **Show Team Profile**). On its own the Team ID grants nothing.
2. Open your own Team Profile, go to **Connected teams**, paste their ID and choose **Request connection**. The row shows "Waiting for them to approve".
3. Their team owner gets a **Team connection** card in their Inbox, under **Requests**. An owner or editor of their team can also answer from **Connected teams** in their own Team Profile, with **Approve** or **Decline**.
4. Once approved, each team sees the other under Connected teams as "Connected". A chip on the row says who asked: **Owner** means they invited your team, **Guest** means your team invited them. Who owns a shared item is shown on the item itself.

- You do this once per company, however much you share later.
- Only an owner or editor can request or approve a connection. Anyone in the team can see the list.
- Nothing arrived? Check that they sent their Team ID (not a user ID or a project ID). The card goes to their team owner.

## Step 2: share one item

Only an owner or editor of your team can share an item.

- **A chat**: when you create a group chat, turn on **Include another organization** and pick connected teams. You can also share an existing group chat from its profile, under **Teams with access**, if you are in that chat. A one-to-one DM, a multi-person DM and a project chat cannot be shared. An external chat is always private.
- **A project**: open the project profile and use **Teams with access** > **Share with a connected team**. Its tasks, task comments, files, task notes, milestones and project chat come with it.
- **A note folder**: in a Team Notes folder's access settings, choose **Share with another organization** (offered only when your team has a connection) and pick connected teams. A shared folder is always restricted to the people let in.
- When you share, you choose what they can do: **Edit** or **View only**; **View only** is pre-selected, so give Edit only when they need to change things. That is the highest role their people can get on that item, and changing it on a share that is already running takes effect at once.
- With **View only** their people can open and read the item but not change it. On a project they cannot create or edit tasks, comment, upload files, edit task notes or post in the project chat. In a chat they cannot post, edit, delete or react. In a note folder they read the notes. With **Edit** they can do these things.
- On a project, people from the other team always join as guests, whatever you chose: they cannot manage its members.
- The other team's owner gets a **Shared with your team** card in their Inbox. An owner or editor of that team accepts it. The person who accepts is let in at once, so they can open the item and decide who else on their side needs it.

## Where the shared item turns up

You find it in your own workspace, in the usual place for that kind of item.

- A shared project appears in your project list, marked as shared. Hover the mark to see which team shared it.
- An external chat appears in your chat list with an **External** badge.
- A shared note folder appears in your Team Notes with a **Shared** badge.
- Only people who were let in see it. Colleagues who were not added see nothing.
- Nothing there? Someone on your team has to add you. Ask whoever accepted the share.

## Each side manages its own people

After a share is accepted, the other team's owner or editor adds and removes their own colleagues on that item whenever they like. They do not need to ask you again.

- Open the item (the project profile, the chat profile or the folder's access settings) and find **Teams with access**. Your own team's row has **Add someone from your team**.
- They can add only people who are members of their own team, and never above the role you allowed.
- You can remove any single person from another team at any time. You cannot add their people for them.
- When someone leaves the other team, they lose access to your shared items at once.

## What stays with the owning team

- Renaming or deleting the shared project, chat or folder, and changing who in the owning team can reach it.
- Sharing it further. A team you shared with cannot pass the item to a third team, and can add only its own members.
- Ending the share. Either team can choose **Stop sharing with this team**. Everyone that team had on the item loses access at once. What they wrote inside stays with the owning team.

## What people from the other team do not see

- Only what was shared: that project, not your other projects; that chat, not your other chats; that folder, not your other notes. Never your member list.
- Search and Genos follow the same boundary. They get results and answers only from the items they were let into.
- Each person's AI use counts against their own plan and credits. Sharing an item does not give anyone your plan.

## Ending a connection

- Stop sharing one item from its **Teams with access** section.
- To end everything, a team owner (on either side) chooses **Disconnect** under Connected teams. This ends every chat, project and note folder shared between the two teams, in both directions. Genos asks you to confirm, then says how many people were removed.
- Either side can end a share or a connection without the other's agreement. You can connect again later, but the old shares do not come back by themselves.

topics.title: Fixes for specific problems
topics.markdown:
## Notifications

- **Nothing arrives at all**: open Settings > **Notifications**. Check that Web notifications is on and that notifications are not paused (a moon on your avatar means they are paused). Then check **Browser permission**. If the browser blocks Genos, no setting in the app can override that.
- **Nothing on an iPhone**: iOS delivers notifications only to the installed app. In Safari, tap Share and choose "Add to Home Screen", open Genos from the home screen, sign in, and allow notifications.
- **Quiet for one conversation only**: it is probably muted. Settings > **Notifications** lists your muted chats and muted items (threads, tasks, notes). Unmute them from there.
- **Too much email**: email has its own switch and categories, apart from in-app and desktop notifications. Every notification email also has an unsubscribe link.
- **A toast instead of a desktop notification**: that is how it works. When the Genos tab is in front, you get an in-app toast. Desktop notifications are for when the tab is in the background.

## Access

- **A project or note won't open**: you are probably not a member. Where it is offered, use request access. The owner approves or declines it from their Inbox.
- **You can't invite anyone**: inviting needs the team owner or an editor. Ask the owner to make you an Editor.
- **The owner has gone quiet**: an editor can choose **Request ownership** in the Team Profile. If the owner does not answer within 30 days, the editor can choose **Take ownership**.
- **An invite link doesn't work**: invites work only for the email address they were sent to and expire after 7 days. If you are signed in as someone else, choose **Sign out and continue**. If it expired, ask for a new invite.
- **Account deletion is refused**: you still own a team that has other members. Transfer ownership of that team from its Team Profile, then delete.

## "Your plan doesn't include…"

- **Connecting an AI app shows "Not on your plan"**: connecting AI apps starts at Core. See Settings > **Plan & Usage**.
- **A connected app shows "Paused"**: your plan does not include connected apps right now. It stays in the list and works again on Core or above.
- **A schedule says it is paused because of your plan**: scheduled reports start at Core. Your schedules are kept and resume when you upgrade.
- **"Webhooks aren't included in your team's plan"**: webhooks start at Core. The team's plan or the team owner's plan counts.
- **An HTML page won't import**: HTML pages start at Core. A page over your plan's size limit is refused too, and so is a page that would take you past your HTML storage.
- **"Your plan keeps up to … skills"**: delete a skill or upgrade.
- **An effort level says "Upgrade to unlock"**: Free goes up to Low, Core up to Medium, Pro and up to High.
- **"You've created all … for this month"**: you reached the monthly task or note limit. It resets on the 1st (UTC).

## Genos and AI credits

- **Out of credits**: Genos says "You've used all your AI credits, so Genos can't answer right now." Choose **Buy credits** for a pack that never expires, or **Upgrade plan**. Monthly credits reset on the 1st (UTC). Settings > **AI credit usage** shows what used them.
- **A long answer stopped partway**: your balance ran low during the request. Buy credits or wait for the monthly reset.
- **Out of asks for today** (when Genos does not use credits): the count resets at midnight UTC. Settings > **Plan & Usage** shows where you stand.
- **It can't find something you just made**: indexing takes a moment. Try again shortly.
- **It says it can't see something you can see**: check that you are in the right team. Each team's content is separate. Only one team can be active in a browser at a time. If a tab says you signed in to another team in another tab, reload it.
- **It answered from something out of date**: fix the note it used. Answers follow the notes.
- **A provider shows "Available soon"**: that provider is not offered yet.

## Signing in

- **Forgot your password**: on the sign-in page choose **Forgot password?** and use the link in the email. This works only for accounts that sign in with email and password. A Google or GitHub account has no Genos password: sign in with that provider.
- **"Too many wrong codes"**: after 5 wrong two-step codes in a row the account is locked for 15 minutes. Each further wrong code makes the wait longer, up to 24 hours. Wait, then try again.
- **"That sign-in expired"**: the code step must be done within a few minutes of entering your password. Enter your password again.
- **Lost your phone**: on the code step choose **Use a recovery code** and enter one of your recovery codes. Each code works once. Then open Settings > **Security**, choose **Turn off** and **Turn on** to set up your new phone, and save the new recovery codes.
- **Lost your phone and your recovery codes**: email support. Support checks that the account is yours before turning two-step verification off.

## Everything else

- **An upload was refused**: the file is over your plan's per-file size limit.
- **The page looks stale or a button does nothing**: reload the tab. A tab left open for days keeps running the code it started with.
- **You deleted a note's content by accident**: open the note's history and restore an earlier version.
- **You deleted the in-app guide and want it back**: it is not re-created by itself. Ask support to restore it.
- Still stuck: genos.support@genosai.dev

topics.title: Genos AI: ask, act, and stay ahead
topics.markdown:
## Where you ask Genos

Genos is the AI in your workspace. You can ask it from three places:

- **Spotlight**, the quick-ask box. Press Cmd-K (Ctrl-K on Windows and Linux) anywhere. Type a few words to search, or write a question and press Enter to ask Genos.
- **The Genos page.** Click Genos in the left sidebar. The page has the same box, a few "Try asking" starter questions, and your Ask history beside the conversation.
- **On the thing itself.** A thread and a note each have an Ask button in their header. It shows a summary first, and then you can ask follow-up questions about that one thread or note. A task or milestone has "Ask Genos about this task" (or milestone) in its ... menu, and that conversation stays with the task. A chat message has "Ask Genos about this message", and you can also select text and choose "Ask Genos about the selected text". Calendar events, projects ("Ask Genos about progress") and sprints have their own Ask entries too.

Genos reads only what you can open yourself: your chats, tasks, notes and to-dos. It cannot see a teammate's private notes or a chat you are not in.

## Asking well

- Type @ to pick a person or a mention group, and # to pick a task, project, note or chat. This tells Genos exactly what you mean.
- Answers link to their sources. Click a link to open the source and check it.
- Under an answer you can Copy answer, Save as note (it goes to My Notes), or Save as task. You can also rate the answer with Good answer or Needs work.
- If you close Spotlight, a thread window or a note window while an answer is still being written, Genos keeps working. When it finishes you get a "Your AI answer is ready" notification. You can turn this off under AI answer ready in Settings > Notifications.

## What Genos can do on your plan

What Genos can do depends on your plan:

- **Free:** Genos answers, searches and summarizes. It cannot create or change anything. If you ask it to make a task or a note, it writes the full text for you to paste.
- **Core:** Genos can also make one change at a time, for example create or update a task, write or edit a note, add a comment, add a to-do, or manage a calendar event once Google Calendar is connected. It can search the web, and it can look back through your past Genos conversations.
- **Pro and Max:** Genos can also make larger changes in one step. For example, it can create a milestone with all of its tasks, update many tasks at once, or set task dependencies. It can also read GitHub pull requests once GitHub is connected.

## Nothing changes without your approval

- Before every change, Genos shows a card titled "Approval required" with exactly what it will create or change. Click Approve or Reject.
- For many changes you can click Edit and fix a title, a date or a sentence before you approve.
- A card marked "Can't be undone" tells you before you approve that this change cannot be reversed.
- After you approve, many changes show an Undo button. Undo puts back what that one change did. It works for up to 7 days, as long as nothing has changed the item since then. Undo cannot take back notifications, messages or emails that were already sent.

## Skills

A skill is a note of written steps with a name. In the box, type / at the start of your question to pick a skill and run it. A skill is either "Read only" or "Read and propose changes". If it proposes a change, the change still waits for your approval. You write and share skills in Settings > Genos > Skills. Skills are there only when your Genos has them turned on.

You can pick and run your own skills and the ones you have installed, and nothing else. In Settings > Genos > Skills there are four lists: **My skills** are the ones you wrote, **Team skills** are the ones teammates share with the team, **Installed** are the ones you installed, and the **Genos Hub** holds every public skill. To use a teammate's skill or a public one, open it in Team skills or the Genos Hub and click **Install**. Uninstall takes it out of your lists again. A few general skills (unread-summary, comments-waiting-on-me, triage, wrapup and weekly-review) are installed for you from the start, and you can uninstall them too. If you run a skill you have not installed, Genos says where to install it. The / list and the schedule's skill list end with **Find more skills in the Genos Hub**.

## Scheduled reports by Genos AI, and dashboard pages

A schedule (Settings > Genos > Schedules, Core and above) prepares a report at times you choose. Most reports are plain: built from your data, with no AI and no credits.

**Scheduled message.** One job is not a report: **Scheduled message** sends a message you wrote to a chat, as you, at the time you pick. No AI is used and no credits are spent.

- Write the message in the same editor as the chat page, with formatting, @ mentions and # links. Images and files cannot be added, and a very long message is refused.
- Pick a group chat (public ones too) or a project chat you are a member of. Direct messages cannot be picked, and the message never goes to your Inbox.
- When it runs, the message appears in the chat from you, like one you sent yourself: mentioned members of the chat are notified, and others in the chat see it as unread. A mentioned person who is no longer in the chat is not notified.
- Genos checks the chat again before every run. If you have left it, or it is archived, nothing is sent; after 3 failed runs the schedule pauses. A run more than 3 hours late is skipped.
- **Run now** sends the message to the chat at once, every time you press it.
- A connected AI app (Claude, ChatGPT) cannot create, change or run a scheduled message. It can only list, pause or delete one.

**Run right away.** When you make a new schedule that runs **One time only**, you can choose **Run right away** instead of a date and time, then click **Run now**. The report goes to your Inbox or the chosen chat at once. If the run fails, no schedule is saved and the form keeps what you typed. A finished one stays in your list, and its name cannot be used again until you delete it.

**Slow reports run in the background.** A report that can take a while (Run a skill, a dashboard page, or a report with AI) does not keep you waiting, for Run now and Run right away alike. Genos says **Started**, the button shows **Running…**, and the report arrives when it is done. If such a run fails, the schedule stays in your list and shows what went wrong. A new Run right away with the same name replaces one that never made a report. A run that was cut off can be started again after about a minute.

**Scheduled job by Genos AI.** Six reports have a **Mode** choice, plain or Scheduled job by Genos AI: What to do today, What is left from last week, Project updates, Milestone updates, Team activity and Dashboard page. Plain is the default. Group chat catch-up and What you did cannot use AI. Run a skill always uses AI, and so does a dashboard page made by a skill, so neither has a Mode choice.

- In What to do today, AI adds one short sentence under a task when its comments explain where it stands. In the other reports, AI adds a short summary (2 to 4 sentences) at the top, written from what the report already lists.
- **AI effort** (Low, Medium or High) appears only when AI is on. The form shows an estimate of the credits one run uses, and each report shows the real figure. Run a skill and a dashboard made by a skill have no estimate. If your plan does not allow the level a saved schedule asks for, the form says which level your plan runs it at.
- AI uses your AI credits. When you have none left, AI cannot be turned on, and a schedule that already has AI on still sends its report, without the AI part. If your Genos has AI reports turned off, the report also arrives without the AI part.

**AI reports in shared chats.** Turning AI on does not widen or narrow who may receive a report: a report goes only to the chats that would take its plain version. The post in the chat includes the AI sentences, but never what the run cost. The cost is shown only to you, in your Inbox. No notification is sent for the post. A scheduled skill is different: it runs on your own skills and data, so it can only be posted in a chat that only you are in.

**Dashboard page.** This report keeps one dashboard page up to date, mostly as pictures. Each kind has its own layout:

- **A milestone:** how much is done, whether it looks likely to finish on time, what is overdue, blocked or without an owner, what is left by due date, and who holds the open work.
- **A project:** its headline numbers, a progress bar for each milestone, the status of the work, the pace of closing and adding tasks, who holds the open work and what needs attention.
- **My progress:** how many tasks you closed compared with the period before, what needs you, and what is next by due date.

"On track", "Tight" or "At risk" is worked out from what was closed in the last 14 days and assumes no new tasks. With too little to go on, the page says nothing. The page's own words are in your app language. A page made by a skill shows the blocks that suit that skill. Choose:

- **Dashboard of:** one milestone, one project, or My progress.
- **Period:** Last week, Last month (the default), Last quarter or Last year. This is how far back the numbers go, not how often the schedule runs. A schedule runs on its own at most once a day (Run now is extra).
- **Focus:** optional, a few words on what the page should look at.

**Links.** The names on the page (the project or milestone in the title, and the tasks it lists) are links: click one to open it in Genos. A page made by a skill can link the tasks, milestones, projects and notes that its run read. Genos writes every link itself, and only to things the page's readers can open. A page you or an AI app saved by hand has no such links.

**Working with the page.** In Genos you can open a "+N more" line to see the rest, sort the due-date list by due date, status or owner, filter the lists by status or person, click a column heading to sort a table, hover or tap a chart to read its numbers, and fold a section by its heading. Nothing you change there is saved. A page made before this gets these at its next run.

The first run saves the page as one HTML page in your notes, and each run after replaces it with the new numbers. Dashboards need a plan that has HTML pages (Core and above). Each run counts toward your plan's HTML page saves per hour (30 on Core, 60 on Pro and above). You can keep up to 10 dashboard schedules.

- **Who can read it.** The page names only tasks that everyone who can read the note may open. A project or milestone dashboard is refused when someone who can read the note is not on that project, and the message names nobody. My progress counts only the projects all of its readers are on, and, when others can read the page, says so on the page.
- **AI summary.** With AI on, the page also gets one short summary. If nothing the page shows has changed since the last AI run (the numbers, the lists and the focus, within 8 days), Genos reuses that summary and spends no credits. If your Genos has AI dashboard summaries turned off, the page is plain. If you have no credits left, the page is plain unless an unchanged summary from the last 8 days can be reused.
- **In your Inbox.** A dashboard run files only the page's name and a **Dashboard page** link. The numbers and lists are on the page. The item still shows what the run cost in AI credits, or why it used none. A run that could not save a page says why.
- **In a chat.** A dashboard schedule that posts to a chat sends a short notice with the title, one line and a link to the page, not the full report. Every person who reads the chat must be able to open the page. If not, the run fails and posts nothing.
- **Where to find them.** Task Stats has a **Custom dashboards by AI** tab. It lists the dashboards your schedules keep up to date (Yours) and dashboards teammates share with you (Shared with you). Only pages you can already open are listed. From there you can open the page, click **Run now**, or add a **New dashboard**, which opens the same schedule form.
- **Save to.** The page can be saved in My notes, one of your own folders or a team folder. Each choice says who can open it. After the first run, the place cannot be changed in the schedule. To move the page, move the note.
- **A page made by a skill.** Choose **Made by**, then **A skill I choose**, pick the skill, and fill in **What to give it** if it needs to be told what to cover, such as a project. The list shows only skills with the `dashboard` tag. Some of the Genos templates have it. To list a skill of your own, make a tag named `dashboard` in Manage tags and put it on the skill. A teammate's skill appears once you install it and the version you installed has the tag. A skill you installed, a Genos template included, appears once you update it to a version that has the tag. A dashboard that already uses a skill keeps running it and showing it, tag or not. Every run uses AI credits, and **AI effort** is shown for it. It can only be saved where you alone can read it. If a run fails, or you have no AI credits left, the previous page stays.
- **Share, edit and delete.** For your own dashboards, the Custom dashboards by AI tab has Share, Edit and Delete. **Share** opens the page's sharing window once the page exists. Every run checks that everyone who can open the page may see its data; for a page made by a skill that means only you. If someone may not, the run fails, and after 3 failed runs the schedule pauses. **Edit** opens the schedule form. **Delete** stops the updates and keeps the page as an ordinary note.
- **From an AI app.** A connected AI app (Claude, ChatGPT) can create or edit a dashboard schedule for you, including the chat it posts to and the place the page is saved. It asks for your approval first, and the same rules apply.

## AI use and credits

- Each ask, summary and AI report uses your plan's AI allowance. Depending on how your Genos is set up, this is either monthly AI credits or daily ask limits. Settings > Plan & Usage shows which one applies to you, and Settings > AI credit usage shows what used your credits.
- When credits run low, a long request may stop partway. When they run out, Genos cannot answer until they renew, or until you buy credits or upgrade. Search still works.

## Settings for Genos

All of these are in Settings > Genos. The gear in Spotlight and on the Genos page opens the first three, plus What Genos remembers.

- **AI model:** which model answers you. On some Genoses this shows an Effort choice (Low, Medium or High) instead. Free can use Low, Core can go up to Medium, and Pro and above can use High. Providers marked "Available soon" cannot be chosen yet.
- **Genos answers:** AI answers lets the Ask button send your question to Genos. When it is off, Spotlight shows search results only. Web search lets Genos use the web when it answers. It is off until you turn it on, needs AI answers to be on, and is included from Core up.
- **How much Genos writes:** Short, Standard or Long. This sets the length of the tasks, milestones, notes and plans Genos writes for you. Chat answers stay short at every level.
- **Genos Assist Schedules (Core and above):** Genos prepares a report at times you choose and puts it in your Inbox, or posts it in a chat. The reports are Group chat catch-up, Project updates, Milestone updates, Team activity, What is left from last week, What you did, What to do today, Dashboard page, and Run a skill (where Skills are on). Scheduled message is not a report: it sends a message you wrote to a group or project chat, as you. Some can run in AI mode, and Dashboard page keeps a living page: see "Scheduled reports by Genos AI, and dashboard pages" above. Core can have 5 schedules, Pro and Max 20. Click Run now to get a report straight away. A schedule pauses itself after 3 failed runs in a row.
- **What Genos remembers:** see and delete your Genos conversations. Here you also choose whether your answers may help teammates ("Let my answers help teammates", off by default for new accounts) and whether Genos notes what your connected AI apps do ("Note my activity", kept 180 days). You can see and delete what Genos stored, and set how Genos weighs things when it ranks your tasks.

topics.title: Notes: personal, team, and shared
topics.markdown:
## Where notes live

- **My Notes**: private to you. Organize them with folders and subfolders.
- **Team Notes**: team folders. Each folder sets who can use it. **Open to the team** means any teammate can read and write in it. **Restricted** limits it to the people you choose. A subfolder can inherit its parent's setting, and every note inside follows its folder.
- **Shared with me**: notes other people shared with you.
- **Task notes**: attached to a task. Members of the project can read and edit them, so plans live next to the work.
- **Chat notes**: attached to a chat or thread, for shared minutes and decisions. People in the chat can read and edit them.
- Star notes and folders to add them to **Favorites**.

## Editing

- The editor is a block editor. It has headings, bulleted and numbered lists, checkboxes, code blocks, tables and images. You can @-mention people and leave comments on text.
- Notes are edited together in real time. Several people can edit at once and see each other's changes as they happen.
- **Version history** keeps earlier versions. Pick one to preview it, and restore it if needed. Restoring adds a new version, so nothing is lost. Only the note's owner and editors can restore.
- **Note templates:** team templates appear next to the built-in ones in the New note menu. A template can be the default for a folder.

## Import and export

- **Import Markdown…** creates a note from a .md file. Choose **Whole folder** to import a folder tree, such as a Notion export. Every subfolder becomes a note folder, every Markdown file becomes a note, and images come along.
- When your Genos has HTML pages turned on, the same dialog also takes a .html file and saves it as an HTML page.
    - The page is shown in a sandbox, and you can't edit it in the note editor.
    - Parts the sandbox blocks, such as scripts or styles loaded from other addresses, are listed when you import.
    - HTML pages need the Core plan or higher. Each plan has a page size limit and a storage quota for HTML pages.
- **Export as Markdown** saves one note. **Export folder as .zip** saves a whole folder as Markdown files with their images, and the zip can be imported back.

## Sharing and access

- Use **Share** on a note to add teammates as **Editor** (can change the note) or **Viewer** (can only read). Only the owner can add or remove people.
- If you open a note you can't see, use **Request Access**. The owner gets the request in their Inbox and can approve it there.
- Search (Cmd+K or Ctrl+K) covers every note you can read.

topics.title: Notifications: in-app, push, and email
topics.markdown:
## The three channels

- **In-app:** your Inbox, plus a toast when the tab is open but you are on another screen.
- **Push:** a desktop or phone notification when the tab is in the background or Genos is closed. Allow it next to "Browser permission" in Settings > Notifications. The device you are looking at does not get a push for news it already shows, but your other devices still do. On an iPhone, notifications work only after you add Genos to your Home Screen.
- **Email:** for when you are away. Genos waits until you have been away for a while, then sends one email with what you missed, not one email per event. Anything you read in the app before then is left out. Email is sent only when your Genos has email turned on.

## Settings > Notifications

- **Web notifications:** the main switch. When it is off, no category notifies you, and that includes email.
- **Pause notifications:** silences in-app, push and email notifications. Pause For 30 minutes, For 1 hour, For 2 hours, Until tomorrow, Until next week, or pick a date and time. Under On a schedule you can pause every day during set hours, for example 17:00 to 09:00. While you are paused, others see a moon on your avatar. The status menu on your avatar also has quick pause choices.
- **Groups:** Chats, Thread replies, Mentions, Task comments, Inbox, and What my AI apps do. Each group has its own switch, and some open to finer switches:
    - Mentions: one switch for each place you can be mentioned (chat message, thread reply, task description, task comment, My Notes, task note, chat note).
    - Inbox: requests and notices, AI answer ready (an AI answer finished after you closed its window), Message reminders and To-do reminders. If you turn a reminder switch off, the reminder still appears in your Inbox, just without a notification.
    - What my AI apps do: what AI apps connected to Genos (for example Claude) do for you. By default you are alerted only for risky actions: deletes, changes to who can open a note or who is in a project, many refused requests, a new app or API key connected, and changes to 10 or more items at once. You can turn on alerts for other actions too.
- **Email notifications:** a separate switch for email, with its own categories. These are on by default: Mentions in chat, Mentions in threads, Mentions in tasks, Mentions in notes, Thread replies, Task comments, and Requests & notices. Being assigned a task also emails you. "Every chat message" and "Reactions" are off by default. A finished AI answer is never emailed. If you turn off a group above, its emails stop too.
- **Muted chats** and **Muted items:** everything you have muted, with an Unmute button for each.

## Muting one conversation or item

- To mute a chat, click the bell in the chat header.
- To mute one thread, task or note, use its header or its ⋮ menu.

## Unsubscribing from email

Every notification email has an unsubscribe link. It turns email notifications off. You can turn them back on in Settings > Notifications.

The old daily email digest and the 8am Inbox digest no longer exist. For a regular summary, set up a Genos Assist Schedule in Settings > Genos (Core and above).

topics.title: Plans, limits, and what happens when you hit one
topics.markdown:
## Where to look

Settings > **Plan & Usage** shows your plan and how much of each limit you have left. **Compare plans** opens the plans page. It compares every plan and has the upgrade buttons. Payment goes through Stripe. **Manage billing** opens the Stripe portal, where you can change plan, update the payment method or cancel.

- **Your plan is your own.** Each person has a personal plan.
- **Team plan.** A team owner can also buy a per-seat team plan (**Team Core**, **Team Pro** or **Team Max**) on the plans page. Only the team owner sees that section. Every member of the team then gets at least that plan. Guests do not.
- **Which plan counts.** Genos uses the best of your own plan and the plans of every team you are a member of. Plan & Usage says "via team …" when a team's plan is the one that counts.
- **First month free.** When your Genos has it turned on, a new account gets Core free for its first 30 days, with no card. Plan & Usage then shows a **Free trial** chip and the end date. Genos also leaves an Inbox notice 5 days before the end and 1 day before. After that you go back to Free. Your data stays. Connected apps and scheduled reports pause until you are on a paid plan again.
- **Changing plan.** An upgrade takes effect at once and you pay the difference. A downgrade takes effect at the end of the billing period. If you cancel, you keep your plan until the end of the billing period.

## What each plan includes

These are the limits your Genos ships with. Plan & Usage shows the numbers that apply to you.

- **Free**: 20 AI asks a day; 50 tasks and 50 notes created a month; 180 days of message history; files up to 5 MB; 30 days of Genos conversation history. Genos answers questions, at Low effort, and sees only your workspace (no web search). No scheduled reports, no connected AI apps or MCP, no webhooks, no HTML notes, up to 3 skills.
- **Core**: 100 AI asks and 25 web searches a day; 200 tasks and 200 notes a month; 365 days of message history; files up to 25 MB; 180 days of Genos history. Genos can take actions for you, at up to Medium effort, and remembers your own history. It can search the web and use Google Calendar. Connected AI apps (MCP), up to 5 scheduled reports, up to 25 skills.
- **Pro**: 250 AI asks and 60 web searches a day; 500 tasks and 500 notes a month; unlimited message history; files up to 50 MB; 365 days of Genos history. Genos can organize whole plans, at up to High effort (tuned automatically), and draws on your team's knowledge. GitHub as well. Up to 20 scheduled reports, up to 100 skills.
- **Max**: 500 AI asks and 150 web searches a day; unlimited tasks and notes; unlimited message history; files up to 100 MB; unlimited Genos history. Same reach and depth as Pro. Up to 20 scheduled reports, unlimited skills.
- **Enterprise**: unlimited asks, searches, tasks and notes; files up to 200 MB; unlimited Genos history. Arranged through **Contact sales**, not bought in the app.

When Genos is not using AI credits, daily caps for premium AI models also apply, by plan.

Before Genos creates or changes anything for you in the app, it shows you what it will do and waits for your approval.

## Other limits by plan

- **Webhooks, per team**: Free none, Core 3, Pro 10, Max 25, Enterprise unlimited. The team's plan or the team owner's plan counts, whichever is better.
- **Scheduled reports, per person**: Free none, Core 5, Pro 20, Max 20, Enterprise 20.
- **Skills you own** (when your Genos has Skills turned on): Free 3, Core 25, Pro 100, Max and Enterprise unlimited.
- **HTML notes** (when your Genos has them turned on): not on Free; there is no limit on how many you keep. Core: up to 512 KB a page and 200 MB of HTML storage. Pro and up: 1 MB a page and 1 GB of storage. Storage counts every kept version of the HTML notes you own (the last 20 of each note). When it is full, a save that would add to it is refused until you delete HTML notes, which frees all their versions at once. Saves are limited per hour across all your HTML notes: Core 30, Pro and up 60. The plan comparison (Settings → Plan & Usage, and the public Plans page) shows the page count (Unlimited), page size, storage and saves per hour. Plan & Usage also shows how much of your HTML storage is used.
- **Connected AI apps and API keys**: Core and up. New connected apps and new API keys per person: Core 3, Pro 10, Max 25. Calls per minute for each key or app: Core 60, Pro 120, Max 240. Calls per day for each person: Core 3,000, Pro 10,000, Max 30,000. Enterprise has no limits. These limits are enforced only when your Genos is set to enforce them. Existing apps and keys keep working.

## AI credits

When your Genos uses AI credits, the monthly credits are your AI limit instead of the daily asks and web searches. Plan & Usage then shows a credit meter instead of the daily counts.

- Monthly credits: Free 5, Core 30, Pro 70, Max 150, Enterprise unlimited. They reset on the 1st of each month (UTC). Unused monthly credits do not carry over.
- These use credits: asking Genos (including running a skill), summaries of threads and notes, the AI sentences in scheduled reports, and AI searches run by your connected apps (Claude, ChatGPT or an API key). A simple question uses fewer credits; deeper work uses more. Searching in Spotlight without asking Genos uses none.
- One request costs at most 5 credits.
- Skills have an effort level (Low, Medium, High). When your balance is low, a skill run starts one level lower and says so.
- Settings > **AI credit usage** shows credits left, what you used this month by job, and recent charges.
- **Buy credits.** The plans page has **Need more credits?** with packs of 10, 50 or 100 credits. Your monthly credits are used first. Bought credits never expire. Packs are not sold on plans with unlimited credits, or when your Genos does not use credits.

## Hitting a limit

- **Low on credits**: you see "Running low — a long request may stop partway." You can still ask. A long request may stop partway when your balance runs out.
- **Out of credits**: Genos says "You've used all your AI credits, so Genos can't answer right now." and offers **Buy credits** and **Upgrade plan**. Summaries stop too. Scheduled reports still arrive, without their AI sentences. Searches by your connected apps still answer, as plain searches without AI, and say so.
- **Daily limits** (when Genos does not use credits): asks and web searches reset at midnight UTC. Nothing is lost.
- **Monthly task and note limits**: you see "You've created all … for this month." The count resets on the 1st (UTC). Deleting a task or note does not give you the count back.
- **History limits hide; they do not delete.** Messages and Genos conversations older than your plan's window stop showing. Upgrading brings them back.
- **Upload refused as too large**: that is your plan's per-file limit, not a broken file. The limit is per file, not per day.
- **Over a count limit** (webhooks, scheduled reports, skills, connected apps, API keys): only new ones are refused. What you already have keeps working after a downgrade. Paused schedules and connected apps work again once you are back on a plan that includes them.

topics.title: Playbooks: how different kinds of work fit Genos
topics.markdown:
## How to read this page

Genos does not assume you write software. Below is one starting shape for each kind of work. Pick the closest one and ignore the rest. They all use the same three pieces, chat, tasks and notes, arranged in different ways.

## Engineers

- Make one project per service or repository.
- Connect GitHub in Settings → Integrations. If your team uses the Genos GitHub App, a team owner or editor installs it once for the team, and then each person presses Authorize. The app is read-only and has no access to code. A connection made the old way shows a note and a Reconnect button. Press Reconnect to switch to narrower, per-repository access.
- To close tasks automatically, "Close my tasks when their PR merges" in Settings → Tasks is on by default for new accounts; accounts made before that keep their own choice, and you can turn it off or on there. When a pull request merges, Genos closes the task whose ID is in the PR's branch name (for example, branch `feature/GEN-42-foo` closes GEN-42). It only closes tasks assigned to you. If a task has several PRs, it closes when the last open one merges.
- Use dependencies for real blockers. If you mark task B "Blocked by" task A, Genos sets B to Blocked. When A finishes, Genos moves B back to Open. "Open task graph" shows what is holding a milestone up.
- Keep design docs in the task's own notes, so the plan stays with the work.
- Ask Genos, for example "what changed in the API project this week?", instead of reading the whole channel.
- To let Claude Code or another AI app work on your tasks, see "Connecting Genos to other tools: API, MCP, and realtime".

## Product and project managers

- Use milestones for dated outcomes, sprints for a regular rhythm, and the task table when you need a spreadsheet view.
- When you rebuild the same filters again and again, use Saved Filters → "Save current filters…". A saved filter is shared with everyone in the project.
- In Customize Task Fields, add the custom fields your process needs and mark them required. Then a task cannot be created without them.
- Task Weight, Team Capacity and Pace on the dashboard help you check whether a plan is realistic.
- For a regular status report, add one in Settings → Genos → Genos Assist Schedules (Core and up). At the times you choose, Genos sends the report to your Inbox or posts it in a chat. Available reports include project and milestone updates, team activity, and what to do today.
- Ask for status instead of putting it together yourself: "what's at risk before Friday?", "what did we close last sprint?"

## Marketing

- Make one project per campaign or channel, with a milestone for each launch date. Tag tasks by medium (blog, email, social, paid), then filter to one medium at a time.
- Draft copy in notes, where several people can write in the same document at once. Put the brief in the task's note, above the drafts.
- Keep approvals in the campaign's chat, so they stay with the work. Turn the decisions that need follow-up into tasks.

## Research and analysis

- Write one note per source or interview, with a folder per study. Make one task per open question. The notes hold the material; the tasks hold what you still owe.
- Genos shows the sources it used for an answer. Click a source to open the exact note before you quote it.
- To ask questions about one long document, use the Ask button in the note's header.
- To bring in existing material, use Notes → Import. "Whole folder" turns a folder tree, such as a Notion export, into note folders and notes.

## Students

- Make one project per course, a milestone per exam or deadline, and a notes folder per subject. Due dates put every course on one calendar.
- To-Do is a checklist for each day, separate from your coursework tasks. It suits study sessions.
- Before an exam, ask about your own notes: "explain what I wrote about elasticity". Use group chats for study groups.

## Operations, back office, and support

- Keep recurring procedures as checklists in notes, with one task per run. Project templates (in the project menu) give each run the same starting text.
- Make one project per process, such as onboarding, invoicing or vendor reviews. Use required fields for details that must never be missing.
- In chat, "Flag for later" keeps a message as a personal follow-up, and "Remind me…" brings it back at a time you choose. Turn requests that need tracking into tasks.
- Every task keeps a history of who changed what and when.
- To move work over from another tool, use "Import tasks from CSV…" in the project's menu. It reads CSV files, including Jira and Notion database exports, and Jira JSON files. A team owner can also bring a Slack export into group chats with "Import from Slack…" in Team Profile.

## Repeat your own steps with Skills

If your Genos has Skills turned on, you can write a set of steps once and run it again later. Open Settings → Genos → Skills and create a skill. A skill can be just for you or shared with your team. To run it, type / at the start of a question in Spotlight and pick the skill. A skill someone else wrote, in Team skills or the Genos Hub, appears there once you install it. A Genos Assist Schedule can also run a skill at set times. It runs the published version, which only reads and changes nothing.

## Whatever the work is

The pattern under all of these is the same. Discussion goes in chat, commitments become tasks, and lasting knowledge goes in notes. Genos reads all three, so you can ask instead of hunting. Start with one real project rather than a perfect structure. The structure is easy to change later.

## A whole company

Setting Genos up for a company with many departments? Read "Organising a large workspace: one team, many departments" and "Setting up Genos for your company: an owner's checklist".

topics.title: Searching and asking: how to get better answers
topics.markdown:
## One box, two jobs

Press Cmd-K (Ctrl-K) to open Spotlight. As you type, Genos searches your messages, tasks, notes and to-dos and shows the results below the box. No AI answer is written while you type. When you press Enter or click Ask, Genos reads the matching material and answers your question. Use a few words to search, and a full sentence to ask.

If AI answers are turned off in Settings > Genos, the box only searches.

## Narrowing a search

- Use the chips under the box to show only Chats, Tasks, Notes, Todos or Genos answers (answers Genos gave before).
- Use the project picker to limit results to one or more projects. Todos and Genos answers have no project, so you cannot use them together with a project filter.
- There is no search syntax. Quotation marks, AND, OR, a leading minus and field:value are read as ordinary words. Use the chips instead. Search matches meaning as well as exact words, so a plain phrase usually works best.
- To find one task, type only its id, for example MIP-890. That task appears at the top.
