- Archived items still show up, marked Archived. Items in a deleted project do not show up.
- You only ever see what your account can open, and so does Genos.

## Asking well

- Name things in the question: @ for a person, # for a task, project, note or chat. "What's left on #WRD before Friday?" works better than "what's left".
- Ask where the material is. A thread and a note each have their own Ask button. A task has "Ask Genos about this task" in its ... menu. These limit the question to that one item.
- Answers link to their sources. Click a link to check it.
- Click a search result to open a preview over your list, so you keep your place. Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) opens the full page instead.
- Save a good answer with Save as note. It goes to My Notes and can be found by search later.

## When it can't find something

- New content takes a moment to become searchable. If something you just made does not show up, wait a little and try again.
- Web search is separate from workspace search. Turn it on under Web search in Settings > Genos. It is included from Core up. When it is off, Genos answers only from your workspace.

## Finding an answer you already had

The Genos page lists your past conversations under Ask history. It shows your 20 most recent conversations. Two things reach past that:

- **Search past asks.** The search box above the list matches every question in a conversation, not just the first one shown on the row. It searches your whole history, not only the 20 rows on screen.
- **Pin.** Click Pin this ask on a row to keep it at the top under Pinned, above Recent. Pinned conversations do not count toward the 20 recent ones. Click Unpin to remove the pin.

How far back your history goes depends on your plan: 30 days on Free, 180 days on Core, 365 days on Pro, and no limit on Max. Pinning does not keep a conversation past that limit. The conversation is hidden, not deleted, and it comes back (still pinned) if you upgrade.

topics.title: Security and sign-in
topics.markdown:
## Two-step verification

Two-step verification makes Genos ask for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app after your password. A stolen or guessed password alone can no longer open your account.

- It applies when you sign in with your email and password. If you sign in with Google or GitHub, turn on two-step verification in that account instead. There is nothing to set up in Genos.
- It is off until you turn it on.

To turn it on:

1. Open Settings > **Security** and choose **Turn on**.
2. Enter your password.
3. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy or any app that makes 6-digit codes). If you can't scan it, type the setup key into the app.
4. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows. The code changes every 30 seconds.
5. Save your 10 recovery codes (**Copy all** or **Download**), confirm with "I have saved these codes", and choose **Done**. They are shown only this once. Keep them apart from your password.

When you sign in, enter the code from the app. If you don't have your phone, choose **Use a recovery code**. Each recovery code works once. Settings > **Security** shows how many are left. **Get new recovery codes** replaces the whole set, and the old codes stop working.

**Turn off**, **Turn on** and **Get new recovery codes** all ask for your password.

After 5 wrong codes in a row, the account is locked for 15 minutes. Each further wrong code makes the wait longer, up to 24 hours.

## If you lose your phone

1. Sign in with your password, then choose **Use a recovery code** and enter one of your codes.
2. Open Settings > **Security**, choose **Turn off**, then **Turn on** again with your new phone.
3. Save the new recovery codes.

If you have lost your recovery codes too, email genos.support@genosai.dev. Support checks that the account is yours before turning two-step verification off. Then you sign in with your password and can set it up again.

## Your password is asked again

Before you add an API key or a webhook, connect an AI app, or give a connected app more access, Genos asks for your password ("Confirm it's you"). After that it does not ask again for 10 minutes. Accounts that sign in with Google or GitHub have no password to enter, so they are not asked.

Genos also emails the address you signed up with whenever an API key, a webhook or an AI-app connection is created on your account.

## Password and email

- There is no way to change your password while signed in. Sign out, choose **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page, and use the link in the email. This works only for accounts that sign in with email and password.
- Resetting your password signs you out everywhere. It also ends your connected AI apps and your API keys. Reconnect your apps and create new keys when you need them.
- Your email address cannot be changed in the app.

## See what happened

- **Your security activity** (Settings > **Account**): your recent sign-ins, sign-outs, data exports, connected accounts and API keys, plus failed attempts to sign in to your account. If something there wasn't you, reset your password.
- **Security log** (Settings > **Developer**, team owner only): sensitive changes to the team, newest first: members joining and leaving, role and ownership changes, invites, API keys, webhooks and alerts. Entries are kept for 365 days.

## Export or delete your account

- **Export your data** (Settings > **Account** > **Download my data**): a JSON file of everything you created: your profile, notes, to-dos, tasks, messages and comments. Team content written by other people is not included.
- **Delete your account** (Settings > **Account** > **Delete account**): type DELETE, and your password if your account has one. Your name, email and profile are erased and you are signed out everywhere. Your private notes, to-dos and AI history are deleted. Teams where you were the last member are closed. Work you did with teammates stays in their workspace, shown as "Deleted user". This cannot be undone.
- You cannot delete your account while you own a team that has other members. Transfer ownership from each team's profile first. To leave one team and keep the rest, use **Your teams** in Settings > **Account**.

topics.title: Settings: every option, and where to find it
topics.markdown:
## Opening Settings

Click Settings in the left sidebar. On a phone, tap More, then Settings. Settings opens on top of what you were doing, so you do not lose your place. It has 14 tabs, in this order: General, Plan & Usage, AI credit usage, Genos, Chat, Tasks, Notifications, Mention groups, Custom emoji, Shortcuts, Security, Account, Integrations, Developer. The "Settings A-Z" page of this manual lists every setting with who can change it, the plan it needs and its default.

## General

- **Appearance:** Theme (Light, Dark or System; System follows your device and changes with it), Color theme (the accent color), and Density (row height in lists and tables).
- **Language:** English, 日本語, Español, Français, 中文 or हिन्दी. Genos also answers you in this language. Text that is not translated yet appears in English.
- **Sidebar:** show or hide Inbox, Chats, Tasks, Notes and To-Do in the left sidebar. Genos is always shown. This syncs across your devices.
- **Privacy & analytics:** Share usage data. It is off until you accept.

## Plan & Usage

Your plan, how much of each limit you have left, and buttons to upgrade, switch or cancel your plan or open Manage billing. Only the team owner sees the Team plan section (per-seat billing for the whole team). Where offered, you can buy one-off credit packs here. Bought credits never expire.

## AI credit usage

Your own AI credits: how many are left, what you used this month, which jobs used them, and recent charges. If your plan counts daily AI requests instead of credits, this tab says so.

## Genos

Settings for the AI (the tab was called Spotlight before):

- AI model (or Effort)
- Genos answers (AI answers and Web search)
- How much Genos writes
- Genos Assist Schedules
- What Genos remembers
- Skills

The Skills card appears only when your Genos has Skills turned on. See the Genos AI page of this manual for what each one does.

## Chat

- **Message layout:** Bubble or Compact.
- **Quick reactions:** your three one-click emoji.
- **Message actions:** pin up to 4 actions to the hover toolbar of messages. The rest stay in the … menu.
- **Double-click action:** whether double-clicking a message adds it to your To-Do list.

## Tasks

- **Quick task creation:** whether the quick-add row in the task table requires the project's required fields.
- **Auto-close on PR merge:** close your tasks when their pull request merges. This needs GitHub connected.
- **Auto-sync to Google Calendar:** add your tasks that have due dates to Google Calendar as all-day events, and Sync existing tasks now. This needs Google Calendar connected.

## Notifications

The main switch, Pause notifications, browser permission, notification groups, Email notifications, and your muted chats and items. See the Notifications page of this manual.

## Mention groups and Custom emoji

- **Mention groups:** a name such as @design that notifies every member of the group when it is mentioned in chat, task comments or task descriptions.
- **Custom emoji:** your team's own emoji. Names use a-z, 0-9, \_, + and -, up to 50 characters. Files must be .png, .jpg, .gif, .webp or .svg, up to 512 KB. Anyone on the team can add one. Only the person who uploaded an emoji can delete it.

## Shortcuts

A list of the keyboard shortcuts. You can change Spotlight and the seven letter shortcuts: select a shortcut's keys, press Ctrl and Cmd (Ctrl and Alt on Windows/Linux) with a letter or number, and reset it any time. The rest are fixed. See the Keyboard shortcuts page of this manual.

## Security

Two-step verification. When it is on, Genos asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app after your password. You get recovery codes for when you lose your phone. It applies to email-and-password sign-in. If you sign in with Google or GitHub, turn on two-step verification in that account instead. See the Security and sign-in page of this manual.

## Account

- **Export your data:** download what you created as a JSON file.
- **Your security activity:** your recent sign-ins, sign-outs, data exports, connected accounts and API keys, plus failed attempts to sign in to your account.
- **Your teams:** leave a team. If you own the team, transfer ownership from its profile first.
- **Delete your account:** type DELETE (and your password, if your account has one). Genos will not delete your account while you own a team that has other members.

## Integrations

Connect Google (for Google Calendar) and GitHub, and choose which repositories Genos can see. The tab is there only when integrations are turned on in your Genos.

## Developer

Connect your AI (Claude or ChatGPT, from Core up), Connected apps, and personal API keys. Creating a key asks for your password again. Team owners and editors also see team keys, connected AI apps and webhooks. Owners also see AI app use and the Security log. Webhooks are not included on Free. See the Connecting page of this manual.

## Your profile (not part of Settings)

Click your avatar and choose My Profile to change your picture, name, job title and status. The status menu on your avatar also lets you pause notifications or choose Set Always Offline.

## Things people look for that aren't there

- Changing your password while signed in: there is no screen for this. Use the forgotten-password link on the sign-in page.
- Changing your email address: not available in the app.
- A time zone picker: Genos reads your time zone from your device. You can see it under Settings > Genos > What Genos remembers > Settings Genos uses.
- Task table columns and sorting: these are in the task table's own column settings, not in Settings.

topics.title: Keyboard shortcuts, in full
topics.markdown:
## Mac and Windows/Linux keys

Where a shortcut uses a modifier key, the Mac key and the Windows/Linux key often differ. Each shortcut below gives both. Settings > Shortcuts shows the same list for your computer, with any shortcuts you changed. The keys below are the built-in ones.

## Changing a shortcut

You can change eight shortcuts: Spotlight (Cmd-K / Ctrl-K) and the seven letter shortcuts for actions. In Settings > Shortcuts, select the keys of the shortcut, then press the new ones. The new keys must be Ctrl and Cmd (Ctrl and Alt on Windows/Linux) with one letter or number. Escape or Cancel stops without changing anything.

- Genos refuses keys that another shortcut already uses, and a few that the system takes (Ctrl-Cmd-Q, F and D on a Mac; Ctrl-Alt-D and L elsewhere). A browser or another app can still take some combinations before Genos sees them.
- A changed shortcut is marked Custom. Use its reset button, or Reset all, to get the built-in keys back.
- Changes are saved to your account. Mac keys and Windows/Linux keys are kept separately.
- On Windows and Linux, a changed shortcut does nothing while you type in an editor or text field, Spotlight included.

The other shortcuts (switching parts of Genos, undo, send, create task, chat arrows, the notes filter, and the table, board and calendar keys) cannot be changed.

## Anywhere in Genos

- Cmd-K (Ctrl-K): open Spotlight. On the Genos page it puts the cursor in that page's own box instead.
- Escape: closes whatever is on top: a menu, a window, or an @ list before the window it is in.
- Switch between parts of Genos: hold Cmd (Alt on Windows/Linux) and tap Ctrl. Each tap moves through Inbox, Chats, Tasks, Notes, Genos and To-Do in the order you last used them, so one tap takes you back to where you were. Add Shift to go backwards. Let go of the held key to switch, or press Escape to stay where you are.
- Cmd-Z (Ctrl-Z): undo a deletion while its Undo message is still showing.
- / on the Notes page: jump to the filter box of the notes list. It does nothing while you are typing in a text field.

## Jump straight to an action

Hold Ctrl and Cmd together on a Mac (Ctrl and Alt on Windows/Linux), then press a letter:

- T: open Tasks and start a new task.
- N: open Notes and start a new note in My Notes.
- X: open your To-Do list.
- C: open the compact calendar.
- M: copy a new Meet link to your clipboard.
- H: open History.
- G: open the task graph for the task you are previewing.

On Windows and Linux these letter shortcuts do nothing while you type in an editor or text field. That way the editor keeps its own Ctrl+Alt keys (Ctrl+Alt+C makes a code block).

## In the Spotlight / Genos box

- Up and Down: move through the results.
- Enter: open the highlighted result as a preview. If no result is highlighted, Enter sends your question to Genos.
- Shift-Enter: start a new line in a long question without sending it.
- Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) a result: open the full page instead of a preview.

## In chat

- Cmd-Enter or Ctrl-Enter: send. Either key works on every computer. Plain Enter starts a new line, so a half-written message is not sent by accident.
- The same keys send a thread reply or a task comment.
- Cmd-click (Alt-click on Windows/Linux) a message: open its thread without leaving the conversation.
- Cmd-Shift-Left/Right (Alt-Shift-Left/Right on Windows/Linux): move between chat tabs. Use Up/Down instead to move through the chat list. These do nothing while you are typing in a field.

## Creating tasks

- Quick-add row: Enter creates the task, and Escape removes the row.
- The full new-task form: Cmd-Enter on a Mac, Ctrl-Enter on Windows/Linux. Unlike chat, only that one key works on each computer.

## Task table

Press Tab to move into the table or out of it. Inside the table:

- Arrow keys: move between cells.
- Home / End: go to the first or last cell in the row. Ctrl+Home / End: go to the first or last cell in the table.
- PageUp / PageDown: move a page up or down.
- Enter or Space: open the cell's editor. Esc: close the editor without saving.

## Task board

Tab moves between columns, one stop per column. Inside the board:

- Arrow keys: move between cards and columns.
- Home / End: go to the first or last card in the column. Ctrl+Home / End: go to the first or last card on the board.
- Enter: open the card's preview.
- Space: pick up a card. Then the arrow keys move it, Space drops it, and Esc cancels.

## Calendar

Tab moves into the calendar and out of it. The month view is one stop. The week and day views have one stop per day.

- Arrow keys: move between days and weeks (month view), or between events and days (week and day views).
- Home / End: first or last day of the week (month view), or first or last event of the day (week and day views).
- PageUp / PageDown: previous or next month (month view).
- Enter: open the day's events or the event. On an empty day, Enter starts a new event.

topics.title: Tasks and projects
topics.markdown:
## Projects

A project holds tasks, milestones and sprints, and it has its own chat. Create one with **New Project** in the Tasks sidebar. Choose Public Project (the team can see it) or Private Project (members only). A private project can also be hidden, so only its members can see that it exists. Each project has a short code, so its tasks get readable IDs like WRD-12.

- **Customize Task Fields** sets which fields are required and their default values for new tasks and milestones. Only the project owner and editors can change these.
- **Custom fields** (Tag, Text, Date or Member) apply to every task, sub-task and milestone in the project. They show in the task panel and as table columns. Owners and editors manage them.
- **Statuses and automation** (the project's "…" menu, owner and editors) lets a project name and colour its own statuses. **Set up statuses** adds the built-ins, including **Ready** (checked and ready to start); then add, rename, recolour, order, set a default, turn off (Ready, WIP, Pending and Rejected) or delete. The statuses are one list, and each says what it **Counts as**: Open, WIP, Blocked, Pending, Closed or Rejected. Board columns, filters, overdue, progress and automations read that, so Ready counts as Open and is not done. You choose it when you add a status, and can change it while no task, milestone or automation rule uses the status (a built-in's is fixed). A status moves up or down among the ones that count as the same. Milestones use the project's statuses too: pick one on the milestone. **Show a column for each status**, at the top of the Statuses tab, replaces the board's columns with one per status for everyone in the project; use it when your team moves work through steps such as Ready or QA. It is off until you turn it on. Its **Automation** tab holds the project's automation rules, described below.
- **Templates:** any project member can add task and milestone templates for the project.
- **Labels:** project labels group projects in the Tasks sidebar, and you can filter the sidebar by label.
- **Import tasks from CSV…** brings in tasks from a CSV file. A Jira or Notion export is recognized, and a Jira JSON export also brings comments. Only the owner or an editor of the project can import.
- **Archiving:** the owner can archive a project. It keeps everything but is read-only until it is unarchived.

## Tasks

- A task has a status (Open, WIP, Pending, Blocked, Closed or Rejected, shown under the project's own names where it set statuses up), a priority, an effort level, an assignee, optional collaborators, start and due dates, tags and a description. Collaborators must be members of the project.
- **Rejected** means a task will not be done. It is finished but not completed: it leaves the progress bar, its sub-tasks read as rejected unless they are already closed, and it no longer blocks other tasks.
- A task has four tabs: Comments, Notes, Attachments and Activity. Activity records every change to the task, and you can restore an earlier description from it.
- **Sub-tasks:** break work down with sub-tasks. A task's page shows the sub-tasks under it.
- **Dependencies:** under Dependencies, mark which tasks a task is **Blocked by** and which it is **Blocking**. Tasks in other projects of the same team can be linked too. While a task has an open blocker, Genos sets it to Blocked. When the last blocker closes, it returns to Open. This only happens if its status is still Blocked; if you set another status yourself, Genos leaves it alone.
- **Task graph:** shows the task tree and its dependencies. Open it with **Open task graph**, or with Ctrl+Cmd+G on a Mac (Ctrl+Alt+G elsewhere) while a task is open in the preview.
- **Task Weight (1–25):** combines priority with time pressure, and a bigger effort level starts the pressure earlier. It drives the **By weight** order in Up Next and **Top by Weight**. Team Capacity and Pace show the load on the project and how fast its work moves.
- **Comments:** comments support @-mentions and reactions.

## Milestones, sprints and views

- **Milestones:** a milestone groups tasks toward one goal and shows their progress. Assign tasks to it, then use **Start Milestone** and **Complete Milestone**. Milestones can sit in folders, and you can star them into Favorites.
- **Sprints:** **Sprint settings** sets a project's sprint length and start day, and can generate upcoming sprints automatically.
- **Views:** the **Sprint Board** shows tasks in columns by status. The **Task Table** is a sortable, filterable grid. Both work from the keyboard (see Settings → Shortcuts).
- **Filtering by status:** in a project with its own statuses, the table's **Status** filter lists them in one list; tick the ones you want. Saved filters remember them.
- **Board columns:** the board has a column per category. With **Show a column for each status** on, it has a column per status, and dropping a card in one gives it that status. A turned-off status keeps a column while cards still have it.
- **Saved filters:** **Saved Filters** saves the current filters under a name. Everyone in the project can use it.
- **Quick add:** in the task table, a quick task needs only a title. To apply the project's required fields there too, turn on Settings → Tasks → Quick task creation.

## Automation rules and guards

A project can have **automation rules**: when something happens to one of its tasks or milestones, Genos can move it to another project, set its status, assign it or add a tag. Rules need the Core plan or higher. The project's owner and editors write them: open the project's "…" menu → **Statuses and automation** → **Automation** → **New rule**.

- **Writing a rule:** name it, then fill the sentence. **When** (**Tasks** or **Milestones**, then: the status becomes, one is created, a tag is added, the assignee changes), **If** (conditions that must all hold; with none, every task or milestone) and **Then** (move to another project, set a status, assign someone, add a tag).
- **Preview before it is on:** **Preview matches** lists the tasks or milestones that match right now and what the rule would do to each, with the reason where it would not. Nothing changes until the next change that fits. Then **Save and turn on** or **Save, keep off**.
- **Order and on/off:** rules are listed in the order they are tried. Move one from its "…" menu or with Alt+↑ / Alt+↓. The switch turns a rule off at once; turning it on shows the preview first. **Recent runs** says what a rule did lately.

- **What sets a rule off:** a task is created, its status or assignee changes, or a tag is added. A rule can also ask for conditions, such as a tag, the assignee, the priority or the milestone.
- **One rule per change:** rules are tried in order, and only the first one that matches acts. What a rule does never sets off another rule.
- **Who it acts as:** a rule runs as the person who last saved it, who must be the project's owner or an editor and a member of the destination project.
- **What moves:** the task takes its sub-tasks, comments, notes and chat card with it. It gets a new ID, and the old ID still works. Tags carry over when the destination has a tag of the same name.
- **What you see:** the task's Activity tab says it was moved by the rule, or why the rule was not applied. The old project's chat gets one line saying a rule moved a task; it names the task and the new project only to people who can open them. The assignee is told.
- **Milestones:** a rule set to **Milestones** reads the milestone's own status, tags and assignees, and cannot use a “milestone” condition (switching a rule to milestones removes it). Moving a milestone moves every task under it and clears the sprint and folder. A rule that assigns someone makes that person the milestone's only assignee.

**Guards.** A rule never moves a task to another team, or to a project that somebody could read who cannot read this one, so a private project's tasks never move to a public one. A sub-task does not move without its parent. A task that rules have acted on several times within an hour is left alone for a while. A rule whose owner can no longer run it is turned off. A milestone with more than 200 tasks under it is not moved by a rule, and its Activity says so. Rules apply to one milestone at most twice within an hour.

## GitHub and Google Calendar

- Connect GitHub in Settings → Integrations. When your Genos has the GitHub App turned on:
    - A team owner or editor installs the Genos GitHub App for the team.
    - Each person then authorizes it.
    - The app is read-only and has no code access. It sees only the repositories chosen in the team's installation.
    - An older GitHub connection shows as a legacy connection, with **Reconnect**.
- Paste a pull request link into a task's Links field to see its state and checks on the task.
- Settings → Tasks → **Close my tasks when their PR merges** closes a task you are assigned to when a pull request whose branch name contains the task ID merges. It is on by default for new accounts (accounts made earlier keep their choice).
- Settings → Tasks → **Auto-sync task due dates** adds tasks with due dates to your Google Calendar as all-day events. It only works one way: deleting an event in Google doesn't change your tasks.

topics.title: Teams, members, and roles
topics.markdown:
## Find your team's settings

Open the team menu and choose **Show Team Profile**. The Team Profile shows the team name, the Team ID, the owner, the members, pending invites, **Connected teams**, and, for the owner, **Sample data** and **Import from Slack**.

## Add people

- **Invite by email.** In the Team Profile, choose **Invite members**, type one or more addresses and choose **Send invites**. Each person gets a link that works only for their own email address. The link expires after 7 days. New members join as Viewers. Only the team owner or an editor can invite.
- **Pending invites** lists the invites that are not yet accepted, who sent each one and when it expires. An owner or editor can cancel one, and the link stops working at once.
- **Request to join.** Someone outside the team can open **Team Management**, search by Team ID and choose **Request to Join**. The request goes to the team owner's Inbox, under **Requests**. An owner or editor can approve it.
- **Guests.** To bring in someone from outside the company for particular projects only, open a project and choose **Invite guests**. A guest sees only the projects they were invited to. Guests do not see your other projects, your member list or anything else in the team. They do not get the team's plan. A project owner or editor can invite guests.
- Each person's time zone comes from their browser. Each person picks their own language under Settings > **General** > Language.

## Roles

Teams, projects and group chats use the same four roles.

- **Owner**: one per team, project or group chat. Only the owner can transfer ownership. In a team, only the owner can remove an editor, disconnect a connected team, remove sample data, import from Slack, buy a team plan and see the team's **Security log**.
- **Editor**: helps run the team day to day. Editors invite and add members, cancel invites, rename the team, change its image, set members' roles (Editor or Viewer), remove viewers and guests, and request or approve team connections. An editor cannot remove another editor or the owner. Make a second person an Editor early, so the team does not depend on one account.
- **Viewer**: the default for new members. Viewers work in the team's chats, projects and notes they belong to. They cannot invite, remove or change members, and they cannot edit the team.
- **Guest**: an outside collaborator invited to particular projects. Guests can work in the projects they were invited to and see nothing else.

In a project, the owner and editors can change **Customize Task Fields** (required fields and default values for new tasks and milestones).

## Remove people, leave a team

- To remove a member, an owner or editor opens the Team Profile and chooses **Remove** next to the person. Genos asks whether to unassign their open work. The owner cannot be removed: transfer ownership first.
- To leave a team yourself, open Settings > **Account** > **Your teams** and choose **Leave**. You lose access to that team's chats, projects and notes. Your account and your other teams stay. The owner cannot leave: transfer ownership first.
- There is no screen for deleting a team.

## Hand over or recover ownership

- **Transfer ownership**: the owner opens the Team Profile, chooses **Transfer ownership** and picks a member. The old owner becomes a regular member.
- **Request ownership**: if the owner has left or stopped responding, an editor can choose **Request ownership**. The owner gets an **Ownership claim** card in their Inbox and can approve or decline it.
- If the owner does neither within 30 days, the editor can choose **Take ownership**. Everyone in the team is told when that happens.
- If the owner declines, the same editor can ask again only after 60 days.
- A team with only an owner and viewers has nobody who can request ownership. Give someone the Editor role before you need it.

## Other team tools

- **Connected teams**: connect with another company's team so you can share single chats, projects or note folders with them. See "Working with another company: cross-team sharing".
- **Import from Slack** (owner only): upload a Slack workspace export ZIP to bring its channels, messages and threads into the team as group chats. People are matched to members by email address. Direct messages are not imported. Files become links back to Slack. **Undo this import…** removes what an import added.
- **Sample data** (owner only): a team created with "Include sample instruction data" gets example projects, chats, notes and to-dos. **Remove sample data…** shows what will be removed and what will stay, then removes it in one step. Anything you added or changed stays.

## Billing for a team

Billing is under Settings > **Plan & Usage**. Each person has their own plan. The team owner can also buy a per-seat team plan (Team Core, Team Pro or Team Max) on the plans page; every member then gets at least that plan. See "Plans, limits, and what happens when you hit one".

topics.title: Tips, shortcuts, and getting unstuck
topics.markdown:
## Fast moves

- **Cmd+K (Ctrl+K)** opens Spotlight from anywhere, to search or ask Genos.
- The letter shortcuts are Ctrl+Cmd+letter on a Mac and Ctrl+Alt+letter on Windows and Linux:
    - **T**: open Tasks and start a new task
    - **N**: create a new My Note
    - **X**: open the To-Do list
    - **H**: open History
    - **G**: open the task graph for the task in the preview
    - **C**: open the calendar
    - **M**: copy a new Google Meet link

    On Windows and Linux they do nothing while you type in a text field.

- **Hold Cmd and tap Ctrl** (Alt and Ctrl elsewhere) to cycle through Genos, Inbox, Chats, Tasks, Notes and To-Do.
- **Cmd+Z or Ctrl+Z** undoes a deletion while its Undo message is still showing.
- **/** on the Notes page jumps to the filter box of the notes list.
- **Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter** sends a message or comment, and creates the task in the new-task form.
- The task table, the sprint board and the calendar work from the keyboard. Tab moves into them, and the arrow keys move inside.
- Settings → Shortcuts lists every shortcut. You can change Spotlight and the letter shortcuts there.
- Paste a Genos link into a message, and clicking it opens a preview over the page, so you never lose your place.
- In a thread, **New task linked to this thread** turns a "we should do this" conversation into tracked work. A thread can have one task.
- The sprint board, the task table and the task graph are three views of the same tasks. Use the one that fits the moment.

## When something seems off

- **Not getting notifications?**
    - Open Settings → Notifications. Check that notifications are on, that they are not paused (a paused person has a moon on their avatar), and that the browser permission says Granted.
    - Check that the chat or item is not muted.
    - On an iPhone, install Genos to the home screen and allow notifications there.
- **Can't see a project, group chat or note?** You may not be a member. Ask the owner to add you, or use **Request to Join** or **Request Access** where it is offered.
- **Something looks out of date?** Reload the tab. A tab you signed in to another team from elsewhere also asks you to reload, because only one team can be active per browser.

## More help

Questions this manual doesn't answer: genos.support@genosai.dev
